MAJOR: `show()` re-executes `architect_review.py gate` via subprocess twice per render (up to 60s each). A supposedly read-only projection is now coupled to an external tool's availability, environment, and latency; a hung/slow reviewer blocks the CLI with no logging or partial-degradation signal (errors are silently swallowed into "cannot render").

The stage table now iterates `STAGES` only and `continue`s on missing entries, so any recorded event whose stage is not in `STAGES` (legacy data, or a new stage introduced by another tool before this constant is updated) silently disappears from the audit table — an observability/append-only-integrity regression versus the previous rank-99 rendering.

`current_stage` is derived purely from "first missing stage", so a stage whose latest event is `fail` (e.g. `gate0: fail`) still advances `current` to the next stage. The header will claim progress past a failing gate; no notion of "blocked at" is represented or tested.

`_parse_recommendation`'s regex and separator normalization couple the renderer to the exact output phrasing of `architect_review.py`. Any wording change ("Overall recommendation:", localized/changed labels) silently degrades to `reviewed (recommendation unavailable)` with no test guarding the contract between the two modules; no test covers the `NOT READY` normalization path required by the acceptance criteria.
MINOR: Current stage is rendered three times (header, section 3, final table row) and the stage checklist duplicates the stage table content — redundancy that will drift as sections evolve.
`_stage_status` defaults non-review stages to `"pass"` when `status` is absent; a silently-defaulted pass contradicts the "never fall back to a pass" principle applied to review stages.
`current_stage` hardcodes status synonyms (`completed/closed/done/delivered`) instead of reusing the backlog's status vocabulary constant; the two will drift.

Empty-item test asserts absence of `"reviewed (recommendation unavailable)"` by relying on no-review-event early return; it does not exercise the `evidence missing` path or `_review_evidence`'s exception branch.
NIT: Hardcoded section ordinals ("## 1." … "## 11.") are duplicated verbatim in the test's expected-order list; extracting an ordered section list would make reordering a single-point change.
`Runs` column appears in the table but the docs describe it only obliquely; worth one line in the lifecycle doc next to the header definition.
`_review_table` compatibility wrapper is retained but apparently unused in-repo; confirm an external caller exists or drop it to avoid a dead seam.
SUMMARY: Solid, well-scoped rendering improvement with good docs sync, test coverage for order/current-stage/dedupe, and correct no-shell subprocess invocation. Top risks: `show` is no longer a cheap read-only projection (two blocking subprocess calls with swallowed failures), the audit table now hides non-`STAGES` events, and `current_stage` ignores failing gates. Recommend addressing the projection/tool coupling and the visibility regression before relying on this view as the enterprise audit surface.
